questions.prompt: What work should happen before the GitHub issue is created?
questions.description: The current request says research, design, model approval, then one GitHub issue. This decides whether code changes are intentionally out of scope for this setup goal.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Research the current repo and pinned NautilusTrader surfaces, write the design and execution plan, obtain external model approvals on that design, then create one GitHub issue. Do not implement production code in this setup goal.

questions.prompt: Which runtime boundary should the design target?
questions.description: The repo already has strategy-local forced-flat behavior, submit admission, runtime capture, and an NT risk engine. A production kill switch can be scoped narrowly or globally.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Target a global bolt-v3 LiveNode/runtime kill switch for configured accounts, instruments, and strategies. It should use NT-native state, submit/cancel/flatten paths, and avoid strategy-local kill logic or bespoke venue calls.

questions.prompt: Which halt triggers should the first production design include?
questions.description: The loss governor is one trigger, but a full kill switch can also support operator and reconciliation triggers.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Include loss-governor breach, manual operator kill, stale or missing NT proof, reconciliation mismatch, cancel/flatten failure, and future trigger extension points. Treat every trigger as a durable latch requiring manual reset evidence.

questions.prompt: What review quorum should count as approved?
questions.description: The plan can request all six Relay reviewers, or a smaller quorum if one provider is unavailable.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use all six Relay reviewers: Claude, Gemini, Kimi, Grok, DeepSeek, and GLM. Treat the design as approved only when each completed review returns no blocking findings; if a model is unavailable, record the failure and ask before lowering the quorum.

questions.prompt: What should the resulting GitHub issue look like?
questions.description: The issue can be a single design-backed umbrella with phases, or only the first implementation slice.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Create one issue that captures the approved full design, production invariants, phased implementation plan, verification matrix, model-review results, and explicit out-of-scope live-capital drill requiring separate approval.
